review_note: Machining losses and the need for operational improvements showed repeated contained pressure; the completed Fradley site closure and machining consolidation were already public and are excluded. Foundry margin declined 80bps for the year, although second-half margin exceeded the prior year. Operating cash flow increased, cash and deposits were £30.8m with no debt, schedules were stable and commercial-vehicle demand was strong, providing strong offsets.

COVID plant closures, extensive furlough, self-isolation disruption, delayed equipment, raw-material inflation and under-recovery represented multiple persistent pressures. Foundry margin fell 350bps to 5.4% and operating cash flow fell £14.2m, partly through lower profit and working-capital movement. Demand recovered toward pre-COVID levels, customers forecast higher volumes, and £36.1m of cash and deposits with no debt provided strong but incomplete offsets.

Dramatic schedule increases caused production rebalancing and second-half inefficiencies, while raw-material, energy and labour pressures were explicit. Foundry margin fell 70bps to 7.3%, partly because of pass-through pricing and disruption. Revenue rose 35.3%, operating cash flow increased to £22.4m, heavy-truck order books were extremely strong and the Group held £35.6m cash with no debt, providing strong quantified contrary evidence.
